items.title: Insauga Reader Poll Puts Parrish Ahead of Crombie Days Before Mississauga Votes
items.summary: Insauga.com reports its own head-to-head reader poll, released less than a week before the Oct. 26 municipal election, shows incumbent mayor Carolyn Parrish leading former mayor Bonnie Crombie among those who responded. According to the outlet, the poll asked only about Parrish and Crombie head-to-head and did not include the other 12 candidates on Mississauga's official mayoral ballot. The outlet reports Parrish is seeking her first full four-year term after winning the city's 2024 mayoral by-election, which was triggered when Crombie left office to lead the Ontario Liberal Party. According to insauga.com, Parrish was elected mayor on June 10, 2024, and took her oath of office on June 24 to serve out the remainder of the 2022-2026 council term. The outlet reports the poll opened and closed within a short window on Oct. 20, reflecting the views of readers who chose to weigh in rather than a scientific sample of the electorate.

items.title: With Debates Behind Them, Four Mayoral Hopefuls Make Their Final Push Before Mississauga Votes
items.summary: Insauga.com reports Mississauga voters head to the polls on Monday to elect a mayor, 11 city councillors and a slate of school board trustees, after a campaign season that featured heated debates among the leading mayoral candidates. According to the outlet, the mayoral race's four main contenders, incumbent Carolyn Parrish, former mayor Bonnie Crombie, and city councillors Alvin Tedjo and Dipika Damerla, are competing within a larger field of 14 hopefuls for the city's top elected office. The outlet reports Parrish and Crombie traded pointed attacks during the campaign's debates, while some polls and campaign watchers suggest Tedjo has recently gained additional support. According to insauga.com, it remains to be seen whether that momentum is enough to turn the race into a close three-way contest on election night. The outlet reports record numbers of residents already cast ballots during advance polling earlier this month, and remaining voters can cast their ballots on Oct. 26 at any location within their own ward. According to the outlet, winning candidates will serve a term running from 2026 to 2030.

items.title: Historic Lakeview Arts Hub Hosts Multiple Dates of The Sunday Antique Market This Fall
items.summary: Insauga.com reports The Sunday Antique Market, known for antiques, art, jewelry and vintage finds, is returning to Mississauga for multiple shows this November. According to the outlet, the market has drawn shoppers for more than 30 years with offerings that range from modernist jewellery and antique silver to vintage paintings, advertising and mid-century decor. The outlet reports the market now takes place at the historic Small Arms Inspection Building in Lakeview, a restored industrial space with high ceilings and large windows that now serves as a local arts and cultural hub. According to insauga.com, the venue sits at 1352 Lakeshore Rd. E., accessible by the QEW or GO Transit's Long Branch station, and offers free parking and free admission. The outlet reports additional shows are scheduled to continue into 2027, with each running from 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. According to the outlet, the market's vendors and curator focus on pieces that feel both timeless and current, reflecting where design is headed.

items.title: Major Track Upgrades Will Shut Down Weekend GO Service on Mississauga's Lakeshore West Line
items.summary: Insauga.com reports GO trains will not run on their normal schedule along the Lakeshore West line in Mississauga, Oakville, Burlington and west Toronto this weekend. According to Metrolinx, work crews will carry out major track upgrades from early Saturday through the end of day Sunday, with some disruption also affecting late Friday night service. The outlet reports that during the shutdown, regular Lakeshore West train service will only run between Niagara Falls and Aldershot GO in Burlington. Metrolinx also noted that ongoing construction from Oct. 23 to 26 at the Long Branch GO station in Toronto's west end will affect GO Transit customers, with no pedestrian or station access during that work. According to the outlet, the station's parking lot will also be closed, and Metrolinx is directing affected riders to use Port Credit GO or Mimico GO instead.

items.title: Sam McDadi Brokerage Breaks Its Own Record Again With Mississauga's Priciest Home Sale
items.summary: Insauga.com reports a private Mississauga estate has just set a new record for the most expensive home ever sold in the city and across the Region of Peel. According to the outlet, Sam McDadi Real Estate Brokerage announced it broke its own previous record, which had been set at the Saint George Mansion on Doulton Drive. Sam McDadi told the outlet the property had been off-market for several months before an interested buyer emerged, ultimately leading to two competing offers. According to McDadi, the sale set a price point comparable to Toronto's affluent Bridal Path neighbourhood, home to celebrities including Drake, which he called a positive sign for the city. The outlet reports the exact price and address are not being disclosed, but McDadi described the custom-built, relatively new property as having a distinctive architectural design and rare amenities. According to insauga.com, McDadi said the sale signals that Mississauga is a city luxury homebuilders and buyers should pay closer attention to.

items.title: Malton's Underinvestment Takes Centre Stage as Seven Ward 5 Candidates Face Off Ahead of Election
items.summary: Mississauga.com reports underinvestment in Malton's community resources, along with property standards enforcement and neighbourhood policing, dominated discussion among Ward 5 council candidates ahead of the Oct. 26 municipal election. According to the outlet, seven of the ward's 10 candidates, including Aruna Anand, Ismail Bawa, Jamie Dookie, Mandeep Singh Dhaliwal, Natalie Hart, Michael Anthony Perretta and Rosemarie Sanchez Sanchez, attended an Oct. 16 public meeting organized by Peel Condominium Corp. 33. The outlet reports Mississauga News also sent candidates questions directly, compiling their written responses alongside statements from the meeting to reflect their positions on local issues. According to the outlet, candidate Aruna Anand said her goal for Malton is to build a safe neighbourhood where everyone feels they belong and takes pride in their homes. The outlet reports Anand called housing affordability a living crisis at the forum, noting Malton's proximity to Pearson Airport makes it a key arrival point for newcomers. According to mississauga.com, her priorities include leveraging airport-area job growth, improving street lighting to reduce crime, expanding youth employment programs and establishing local police office hours for residents.

items.title: Intergenerational Fairness Debate Erupts Over Tedjo's Senior Property-Tax Freeze Proposal
items.summary: The Toronto Star reports Mississauga mayoral candidate Alvin Tedjo's proposal to permanently freeze property tax increases for seniors has become a flashpoint in a municipal election already centred on affordability. According to the outlet, opponents argue the plan would shift the cost of running city services onto younger property owners already struggling with heavy mortgages. The Star reports Tedjo pointed to a similar program in British Columbia as his inspiration, though that program has drawn criticism for benefiting seniors who don't actually need the assistance and has become a provincial election issue there. According to the outlet, Tedjo said his version would aim to strike the right balance, helping cash-poor seniors stay in their homes without burdening young taxpayers, and noted that he has young children of his own. The Star reports mayoral rival Dipika Damerla called the proposal misleading, warning it could fuel intergenerational unfairness unless it were targeted specifically at low-income seniors. According to the outlet, Trent University municipal finance expert Harry Kitchen offered a blunt assessment of the proposal's feasibility.
